# Error codes and what to do about them

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-skill-references.ts from the adapters and the error catalog. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every Agentship error carries `code`, `message`, `retryable` and usually a `remediation`.
Read the remediation first: it is written for you to relay. Codes are grouped by family, so
you can react to a class of failure without knowing every member.

## AUTH_*

- `AUTH_MISSING_CREDENTIALS` — No credentials for that store. Run agentship_configure_auth and walk the user through the console steps.
- `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` — The stored credential is malformed. Ask the user to create a new key and store it again.
- `AUTH_KEYRING_UNAVAILABLE` — No OS keyring on this machine. Use the credential environment variables instead (agentship_setup_status lists them).
- `AUTH_KEYRING_ERROR` — The keyring exists but refused the operation. Ask the user to unlock it.
- `AUTH_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND` — The named credential profile does not exist. Use one that does.
- `AUTH_ENV_INCOMPLETE` — Some credential environment variables are set and others are missing. Set the whole group or none.
- `AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED` — The credential works but lacks permissions. Apple: create the key with the App Manager role. Google: check the service account in Play Console Users and permissions.

## TOOL_*

- `TOOL_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` — Agentship supports macOS and Linux on x64 and arm64.
- `TOOL_UNKNOWN` — Internal: a tool name Agentship does not manage.
- `TOOL_LOCK_ENTRY_MISSING` — The pinned toolchain has no build for this platform.
- `TOOL_NOT_INSTALLED` — Tell the user to run "agentship setup --yes".
- `TOOL_DOWNLOAD_FAILED` — Network problem while downloading a managed binary. Retry, then check connectivity.
- `TOOL_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH` — A downloaded binary did not match its pinned hash. Stop and report it: this is a supply-chain signal, not a retry.
- `TOOL_SIZE_EXCEEDED` — A download was larger than the pinned size. Same handling as a checksum mismatch.
- `TOOL_LOCK_TIMEOUT` — Another Agentship process is installing. Wait and retry.
- `TOOL_HEALTHCHECK_FAILED` — A freshly installed binary did not run. Tell the user to run "agentship doctor".
- `TOOL_INSTALL_CORRUPT` — The installation is damaged. "agentship doctor" repairs or reinstalls it.
- `TOOL_ROLLBACK_UNAVAILABLE` — No previous version to roll back to. Run "agentship update --yes".
- `TOOL_EXEC_FAILED` — A managed binary failed. Read the error detail; it carries the store message.
- `TOOL_TIMEOUT` — A store call took too long. Retry; if it persists, check the store status page.
- `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE` — A store answer was too large to process. Narrow the request.
- `TOOL_INVALID_OUTPUT` — A managed binary returned something unexpected. "agentship doctor", then report it.
- `TOOL_VERSION_DRIFT` — The installed binary is not the pinned version. Run "agentship update --yes".

## BUILD_*

- `BUILD_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` — This machine cannot produce that artifact at all (an .ipa needs macOS). Build it elsewhere and point release.artifacts at the file; everything else Agentship does still works here.
- `BUILD_TOOL_MISSING` — A build tool the project needs is not installed (Xcode, a JDK, the Flutter SDK). The remediation names the exact one; Agentship does not install it for the user.
- `BUILD_UNSUPPORTED_PROJECT` — Agentship has no builder for this project shape — usually an Expo managed app with no ios/ or android/ folder. Never run "expo prebuild" for the user: it regenerates those folders and can overwrite native changes. Offer the two documented ways out.
- `BUILD_INPUT_REQUIRED` — The build needs a value the manifest does not have (a scheme, a build number). Ask the user for exactly the listed paths and write them into .agentship/agentship.yaml.
- `BUILD_FAILED` — The build tool failed. The error carries a diagnosis and the path of the full log; relay those. Never paste a build log into the conversation.
- `BUILD_SIGNING_FAILED` — Code signing failed. Read the remediation: it distinguishes a missing certificate, an unregistered bundle id, unaccepted agreements and a wrong keystore password, and each has a different fix.
- `BUILD_ARTIFACT_INVALID` — The build produced nothing, or something whose version contradicts the release. Do not upload it: align the manifest with the project, or stop hard-coding the version in the project.

## STORE_*

- `STORE_UNAUTHORIZED` — The store rejected the credentials. Re-check them with agentship_setup_status.
- `STORE_NOT_FOUND` — The store does not have that resource. For a missing app record, the create-app pending operation is the way forward.
- `STORE_RATE_LIMITED` — The store throttled us. Retryable: wait and try again.
- `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` — The store is down or in maintenance. Retryable.
- `STORE_VALIDATION_FAILED` — The store rejected the content. Read the message, fix the manifest, plan again.
- `STORE_CONFLICT` — The remote state moved under us (a version already in review, an expired edit). Plan again and show the new diff.
- `STORE_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` — No API for this. Continue through agentship_pending.
- `STORE_REJECTED` — The store refused for policy reasons. Relay the message; do not retry blindly.

## ANALYZE_*

- `ANALYZE_PATH_NOT_FOUND` — The path does not exist. Ask the user for the repository root.
- `ANALYZE_NOT_A_DIRECTORY` — Pass the repository root, not a file.
- `ANALYZE_FRAMEWORK_UNKNOWN` — Agentship could not identify the framework. Ask the user what it is and fill the manifest by hand.
- `ANALYZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — The repository hit a scan limit. Results are partial; say so.
- `ANALYZE_UNREADABLE` — The repository could not be read. Check permissions.

## PLAN_*

- `PLAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED` — Show the diff to the user and pass the approved action id to agentship_apply.
- `PLAN_APPROVAL_STALE` — The content changed after the approval. Plan again, show the new diff, ask again. Never reuse the old id.
- `PLAN_INPUT_REQUIRED` — A manifest value is missing. Ask the user for exactly the listed paths and write them into .agentship/agentship.yaml.
- `PLAN_CONFLICT` — The plan no longer matches the store. Plan again.
- `PLAN_JOURNAL_CORRUPT` — The journal is unreadable, so Agentship verifies against the store instead of trusting it. Nothing is executed blindly; call agentship_resume.
- `PLAN_NOT_FOUND` — The plan id is not the current one. Call agentship_plan and use the new id.
- `PLAN_STEP_FAILED` — An action failed mid-run. Read the outcome, fix the cause, call agentship_resume.
- `PLAN_LOCKED` — Another apply is running for this project. Wait for it instead of forcing anything.

## CONFIG_*

- `CONFIG_INVALID` — Agentship configuration failed validation. The message names the file to fix.
- `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` — Something Agentship needs does not exist yet — usually the manifest. Run agentship_analyze first.
- `CONFIG_HOME_UNWRITABLE` — Agentship cannot write to ~/.agentship. Check permissions or set AGENTSHIP_HOME.
- `CONFIG_MANIFEST_INVALID` — .agentship/agentship.yaml failed validation. The error details name the fields; fix them and plan again.
- `CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` — The file was written by a different Agentship. Run "agentship update --yes".

## Rules

- Never invent a fix that contradicts the remediation.
- `retryable: true` (rate limits, store outages, download failures) is the only case where
  repeating the same call unchanged is reasonable.
- A failed apply never needs cleaning up by hand: call `agentship_resume`, which re-reads the
  journal and the store and continues from the real state.
